2027-01-01.title: Mary, the Holy Mother of God · Solemnity · Octave Day of Christmas
readings: The Lord bless you and keep you
May God be gracious to us and bless us

Mary treasured all these words; the child was named Jesus
2027-01-01.alt: Holy day of obligation in many countries (check your diocese). World Day of Prayer for Peace. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-01-01.verse: But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.
theo: The Church begins the civil year not with fireworks but with a mother. On the eighth day of Christmas she proclaims the oldest Marian title of all: Mary is Theotokos, Mother of God. The Council of Ephesus (431) defended this title against those who wished to call her only the mother of the man Jesus. The Church answered: the child she bore is one Person, the eternal Son, true God and true man; so she is truly the Mother of God (CCC 495). To honour Mary is to confess who Jesus is.

St Paul gives the shortest Christmas creed in the New Testament: “when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law.” God's eternity enters time through the yes of one woman. And the purpose is our adoption: “so that we might receive adoption as children.” Because of Mary's Son, the Spirit cries in our hearts, “Abba! Father!” The first reading puts the priestly blessing of Aaron on our lips for the new year: “The LORD bless you and keep you.” In Christ that blessing has a face.

In the Gospel the shepherds find “Mary and Joseph, and the child lying in the manger.” Everyone is amazed, “But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.” On the eighth day the child is circumcised and receives the name Jesus, “the name given by the angel”. The year opens with a Name that means “the Lord saves”, and with a mother who keeps God's deeds in her heart. St Paul VI made this day the World Day of Peace; Mary, Queen of Peace, teaches us to receive the Prince of Peace.
conn: Greek for “God-bearer”. The Council of Ephesus (431) proclaimed it; the people of Ephesus carried the bishops through the streets with torches in joy (CCC 466, 495).
Numbers 6:24–26 is the oldest biblical text found outside the Bible: two small silver scrolls from about 600 BC found at Ketef Hinnom in Jerusalem carry these words.
Circumcision on the eighth day (Genesis 17:12; Leviticus 12:3) brought a boy into the covenant. Jesus, born under the Law, keeps it faithfully in order to redeem those under the Law.
Yeshua means “the LORD saves” (Matthew 1:21). Every knee bends at this name (Philippians 2:10). The Church keeps the Most Holy Name of Jesus as an optional memorial on 3 January.
St Paul VI instituted it in 1968. Each year the Pope publishes a message for 1 January.
The Greek word in Luke 2:19 means “to throw together”: Mary puts events side by side and seeks their meaning in God. She is the model of meditation on the Word.
altar: At the altar we receive the same Body that Mary carried in her womb and held in her arms. Each Communion makes us, in a small way, bearers of God.
The priest ends Mass with a blessing. Today let it echo the blessing of Aaron: the Lord bless you and keep you through this whole year.

Mary is the type of the Church: virgin and mother, she bore Christ, as the Church brings forth children by water and the Spirit.

2027-01-01.prayer: O God, who through the fruitful virginity of Blessed Mary bestowed on the human race the grace of eternal salvation, grant, we pray, that we may experience the intercession of her, through whom we were found worthy to receive the author of life, our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son. Who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen.

family.explain: The shepherds found baby Jesus with Mary and Joseph. Mary kept everything in her heart and thought about it. On the eighth day the baby was named Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for peace in the world and in our home this year.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing God did for our family last year?”

illus: A grandmother in Thrissur kept a small diary for fifty years. Each night she wrote one line: what God had done that day. When she died, her grandchildren read it and found a whole family history of grace: births, illnesses healed, quarrels mended. She had pondered, like Mary, and her family discovered how faithful God had been.

pm.open: Holy Mary, Mother of God, you kept the words of your Son in your heart. On this first day of the year we gather with you around Jesus. Lord, bless us and keep us, and give us your peace. Amen.
share: “The LORD bless you and keep you” (Numbers 6:24). Which blessing of last year am I most grateful for?
Mary pondered all these things (Luke 2:19). How can I make silence for God this year?
God sent his Son so that we might be his children (Galatians 4:4–7). What does it mean to me to call God Abba?
pm.resp: Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us.
interc: For the Church, that like Mary she may bring Christ to the world.
For peace among nations, and for an end to war and violence.
For our families, that the Lord may bless and keep them all through this year.
For mothers, especially those who are expecting a child or who grieve a child.
For our group, that we may ponder the Word each day.
pm.close: Lord God, you gave us your Son through the Virgin Mary. Through her prayers bless this new year, keep us in your love and give us your peace. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a happy and holy new year to you all. The Church begins the year by looking at a mother and her child. On the eighth day of Christmas we celebrate Mary, the Holy Mother of God.

Why such a great title? Because of who her Son is. The child she bore is not a man in whom God lived for a while; he is the eternal Son of God who became man in her womb. One Person, truly God and truly man. That is why the Council of Ephesus in 431 declared that Mary is Theotokos, Mother of God. When we honour Mary, we are really confessing our faith in Jesus.

St Paul says that when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman (Galatians 4:4). Time reached its fullness not in an empire or a palace but in a young woman of Nazareth who said yes. And the purpose of it all is that we might receive adoption as children. Because Mary's Son became our brother, we can call God Abba, Father.

In the Gospel the shepherds hurry to Bethlehem and tell everyone what the angels had said. All who heard were amazed. But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart (Luke 2:19). Amazement passes; pondering stays. Mary teaches us not to rush from one event to the next, but to keep God's deeds in our heart and seek their meaning.

On the eighth day the child receives his name: Jesus, the Lord saves. The first reading gives us the blessing that God told Aaron to place on the people: the Lord bless you and keep you; the Lord make his face shine upon you; the Lord give you peace (Numbers 6:24–26). In Jesus, God's face has shone upon us; in Jesus, God's peace has a name.

So let us begin this year with Mary. Let us ponder each day what God is doing. Let us call on the holy name of Jesus. And let us be people of peace, for today is also the World Day of Peace. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us this year. Amen.
kids: Children, today we say Happy New Year to Mother Mary! She is the Mother of Jesus, and Jesus is God, so she is the Mother of God.
Mary kept everything about Jesus in her heart. Tonight, before you sleep, tell Jesus one good thing that happened today.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a blessed new year to all of you. On the eighth day after his birth the Child was circumcised and was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived (Luke 2:21). The name means the Lord saves. God chose it himself.

In the Bible a name is a mission. The angel told Joseph: you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins (Matthew 1:21). Every time we say the name of Jesus, we confess what he came to do.

Paul tells us that because Jesus humbled himself to the cross, God gave him the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend (Philippians 2:9–10). That is why we bow our heads at his name.

Peter, standing before the council, said: there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven by which we must be saved (Acts 4:12). We do not know what this year will bring. But we know the name in which we will face it.

So let us begin the year as the Church begins it: in the name of Jesus. Let it be the first word on our lips in the morning and the last at night. And may the Lord bless us and keep us in his name throughout this year. Amen.

opts.resolve: I will entrust this year to Mary, Mother of God, and keep a habit of thanksgiving each night.
homily: Dear friends, today the Church greets Mary with her greatest title: Mother of God. In the year 431 the bishops gathered at Ephesus defended this title, because the Child she bore is not a man who later became God, but the eternal Son of God made man. Honouring Mary protects the truth about Jesus.
Paul says: when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman (Galatians 4:4). God did not come among us from nowhere. He came through a mother, through a family, through a people.

When the shepherds told what they had seen, Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart (Luke 2:19). She did not understand everything, but she kept it and turned it over in prayer. That is a good way to live a year.
Paul adds: because you are children, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, Abba, Father (Galatians 4:6). Through Mary's Son we become children of God.

So let us begin the year with her. Let us ask Mary, Mother of God, to keep our families, and let us learn from her to ponder each day what God has done. And may the Lord bless us and keep us, and give us peace. Amen.

concl: Mary gives us Jesus, and Jesus makes us children of the Father.
Let us begin the year with her, blessed and at peace.
